archetype.name: Gunslinger (downfield-first)
archetype.definition: A quarterback who lives on aggressive throws beyond the sticks, piling up efficiency in chunks and accepting a high interception rate as the price, as Darnold has throughout his career.

report.headline: The deep ball survived; everything underneath it, and his protection, did not.
report.take:
Darnold arrived in Seattle off two strong years. In 2025 he ranked 5th in yards per attempt (8.49) and 9th in CPOE. In 2024 he was top 10 in yards, touchdowns and rating. Both seasons were built on attacking downfield, and both came with plenty of interceptions (ranked 50th and 61st in picks). That second trait never left. What has left in 2026 is everything that made the turnovers affordable. His EPA per dropback is -0.061 (35th of 55), his CPOE is -2.01, and his completion rate is down 7.5 points from last year. On paper this looks a lot more like his Jets and Panthers seasons than his last two.

The depth split explains it. Throwing 20+ yards he has been excellent: +0.906 EPA a play, a +15.3 CPOE, two touchdowns and no picks on 20 throws. Everything at 10+ air yards runs at +0.387. Under 10 yards the offense falls apart at -0.171 a play. The throws behind the line are the worst of it: they complete 71.1% of the time and still lost 17 points of EPA. A screen game that completes passes and still bleeds value points to blocking, not to the passer. That fits the rest of the picture. He is under pressure on 30.7% of dropbacks (44th of 45), the offense's hit rate allowed ranks 29th, and the run game ranks 30th. The result is third downs at an average of 8.3 to go, converted just 30.6% of the time. Jaxon Smith-Njigba is the one reliable answer (+0.467 EPA per target on 68 targets). AJ Barner and Rashid Shaheed have both been negative on a combined 54 looks.

Some of what the numbers show is less damning than it looks, and some is worse. His bad-throw rate is up only 1.1 points from last season, and Next Gen's CPOE has him slightly positive (0.77). So the accuracy collapse is partly about the throws he is being asked to make and who is catching them, not just his ball placement. His aggressiveness jumped 5.5 points to 18.66%, a quarterback pushing to make plays the structure isn't creating. The worse part is when he has been costly. In one-score games he is at -0.175 EPA a play with seven of his nine picks. His positive work comes mostly when trailing big or leading big. All nine interceptions also count as turnover-worthy, so none of that is bad luck to wait out.

Where this goes depends heavily on the bodies around him. The Kansas City game shows the ceiling: pressured on 6.7% of dropbacks, +7.6 EPA. The other games show the floor. Right now he is listed out with quad and rib injuries, though he suited up for Monday's unofficial practice. His line is also missing Charles Cross and Quenton Nelson, so the next stretch tilts toward the floor unless the protection gets healthier.

strengths.title: Still lethal beyond 20 yards
strengths.body: His deep throws have been the most efficient part of Seattle's offense: high-EPA, well above expected completion, and no interceptions. It matches who he was in 2024-25, so it's a real skill and not a fluke. Twenty attempts is a small sample, though, and the per-play figure will cool even if the trait holds.

strengths.title: The Smith-Njigba connection carries the offense
strengths.body: Smith-Njigba has drawn by far the most targets and turned them into strongly positive EPA. That is the one route-runner Darnold consistently trusts and hits. Because it rests on volume and an established pairing, it should hold. It also means the passing game narrows badly whenever he is covered.

strengths.title: Scrambles that move the chains
strengths.body: He doesn't run often, but when the pocket breaks down his scrambles have been productive, with six first downs on nine tries. It is a useful escape valve behind a leaky line. It won't happen often enough to change his profile.

concerns.title: The short game is a liability
concerns.body: Throws under 10 yards are deeply negative, and the screen game loses value even when it completes. That's a blocking-and-structure problem as much as a passer problem. Still, his CPOE on short throws is also poor, and the middle of the field has produced no touchdowns and three picks. Until the line stabilizes, the easy throws won't be easy.

concerns.title: Pressure is drowning the offense
concerns.body: He is among the most pressured quarterbacks in the league, the offensive hit rate ranks near the bottom, and third downs have been a disaster. His pressure-to-sack rate is actually decent, so this is mostly what is in front of him, not him holding the ball. With both starting tackles banged up, it isn't getting better soon.

concerns.title: Interceptions are a career constant
concerns.body: His interception rate ranks 48th of 55. That would be alarming as a new problem, but he finished near the bottom in picks even in his best seasons. The difference now is that the efficiency which used to pay for them is gone. Expect the picks to continue; whether they are tolerable depends on the downfield game.

trend.note: His game-to-game EPA swings hard: strong against Washington and Kansas City, deeply negative against San Francisco, Denver and Chicago. Over the last three games his volume rose but his accuracy fell (CPOE -5.9). Health interruptions have kept him from settling in.

nextGame.headline: A rush that can't finish meets a line missing tackles
nextGame.body:
San Francisco's defense is the strangest possible fit for him. It has the league's lowest sack rate, which is the one relief for a quarterback this heavily pressured. But it ranks 5th against deep throws, the only area where Darnold has been consistently good, and 20th on short throws, the area where he has been worst. Its pass defense overall is middling (16th). The first meeting still went badly: 40% pressure, five sacks, two picks and -9.7 EPA. The 49ers' offense leads the league in pass EPA and the Book has them -3 at home with a 46.5 total, so Seattle may need volume to keep up. That pushes Darnold toward the high-attempt, higher-risk games where his picks pile up.

Availability drives everything. Darnold is listed out with quad and rib injuries but suited up for Monday's unofficial practice, and his projected return is this game's date, an estimate rather than a promise. If he can't go, Drew Lock has handled Seattle's other starts. Up front, Cross and Nelson are out, also with estimated returns this week, and Abraham Lucas is questionable. Possibly both starting tackles out turns a manageable pass rush into a real threat. On the other side, linebacker Dre Greenlaw is out, which softens the middle where Darnold has struggled. Corner Deommodore Lenoir is questionable, and if he sits it opens room for Smith-Njigba. The early forecast shows light drizzle and modest wind, not enough to matter yet.

keyMatchups.title: Patched line vs non-finishing rush
keyMatchups.body: San Francisco rarely converts pressure into sacks, but it pressured Darnold heavily in Week 5. With Cross and Nelson out, the question is whether backups can keep the pocket clean enough for him to set his feet and throw downfield.

keyMatchups.title: His deep ball vs SF's deep defense
keyMatchups.body: His best area runs straight into one of the league's better deep defenses. If San Francisco takes away the 20-yard shots, he is left with the short game that has been failing all year.

keyMatchups.title: Smith-Njigba against the WR1 matchup
keyMatchups.body: San Francisco has been fairly stingy per play against WR1s, but those receivers have still slightly beaten their usual output. A Lenoir absence would tilt this toward Seattle's one dependable target.

nextGame.watch: Whether Darnold practices fully and whether Seattle gets a starting tackle back. If both happen, his downfield game has a chance; if not, expect the Week 5 script again.

restOfSeason.body:
The downfield efficiency and the Smith-Njigba connection are real and should hold. The interception rate is a career trait, so don't expect it to fall far. The short-game collapse and the pressure load are tied to an offensive line now missing starters and a run game near the bottom of the league. Seattle's defense is good enough to keep games close, so the team won't need him to throw 40 times every week. But close games are where he has been costliest. A realistic expectation is roughly league-average yardage with a below-average turnover profile, roughly 200-245 passing yards and 0.8-1.3 interceptions a game.

There is upside. If the line gets healthy and the pressure rate drops toward normal, his 2025 form shows he can push back toward positive EPA quickly. Kansas City showed what a clean pocket looks like. If he keeps missing time or plays hurt behind backups, the low end of these ranges is more likely.
swingFactors: Return of Cross, Nelson and Lucas up front
His own quad/rib recovery and snap share
Whether a second receiver beyond Smith-Njigba produces

confidence.note: Over 200 attempts plus a long career baseline, but injuries to him and his line cloud the next few weeks.
